chunks.arabic_text: عُيُونُ الْأَخْبَارِ: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى الْعَطَّارُ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي الْخَطَّابِ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ، عَنْ أَبِي الْجَارُودِ، عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ، عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْأَنْصَارِيِّ قَالَ

translations.en: Uyun al-Akhbar: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi al-Jarud, from Abi Ja'far, from Jabir ibn Abdallah al-Ansari who said:

chunks.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى فَاطِمَ عَلَيْهَا السَّلَامُ وَبَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا لَوْحٌ فِيهِ أَسْمَاءُ الْأَوْصِيَاءِ فَعَدَدْتُ اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ آخِرَهُمُ الْقَائِمُ ثَلَاثَةٌ مِنْهُمْ مُحَمَّدٌ وَأَرْبَعَةٌ مِنْهُمْ عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ

translations.en: I entered to meet Fatima (peace be upon her) and found a tablet in front of her which had the names of the Awsiya (Heirs). I counted twelve, the last of them being the Qaim. Three of them were Muhammad and four of them were Ali, peace be upon them.

en.summary: This narration from *Ayn al-Akhbar* highlights Fatima al-Zahra’s (peace be upon her) role as a living repository of divine knowledge, presenting a tablet that enumerates the twelve Imams, thereby establishing the doctrine of *Ismah* (infallibility) and *Nass* (designation) within Shia theology. The specific mention of three Muhammads and four Alis underscores the continuity of prophetic lineage, while the inclusion of Al-Qa'im as the final Imam affirms the eschatological expectation of the Mahdi. This account serves as a crucial link in the chain of transmission, connecting the Prophet’s household directly to the subsequent Imams.
en.seo_question: What did the tablet in front of Fatima (peace be upon her) list regarding the successors?

key_terms.الْأَوْصِيَاءِ: The Heirs or Successors, referring to the Imams
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qaim (The Riser), a title for the twelfth Imam
